relevant_findings.finding: Soffit is the horizontal underside of the eave overhang along the roofline. Per PaintScope Exterior Key Catalog, soffit is measured in square feet (PS_EXT_SURFACE_SF.SOFFIT_FIELD) from eave depth x roofline perimeter length. This is an SF-based spec like siding, NOT LF-based like trim. The defining characteristic is that ALL work is overhead — the painter works above their head for every task.

relevant_findings.topic: Soffit substrate types in new construction
relevant_findings.finding: Three primary soffit substrate types in NC: (1) Wood — tongue and groove (T&G) boards or plywood panels. Porous, requires sealing and primer. (2) Fiber cement — HardieSoffit panels. Ships with factory primer (transit protection only). Non-porous face, porous cut edges. (3) Vinyl — factory-colored PVC panels. Often NOT painted. When painting is required, vinyl soffit requires bonding primer and LRV restrictions identical to vinyl siding (LRV 55+ standard, VinylSafe for darker colors).

relevant_findings.topic: Overhead work penalty is the dominant production factor
relevant_findings.finding: Soffit painting is 100% overhead work. Every task — prep, prime, paint — is performed with arms extended above the head. This dramatically reduces production rates compared to vertical wall work. Industry data shows overhead work reduces production rates by 25-40% versus vertical surfaces at the same height tier. The overhead penalty stacks ON TOP of the height modifier, creating a double penalty. This is the single most important cost driver for soffit work.

relevant_findings.topic: Brush/roll is the dominant application method even on spray projects
relevant_findings.finding: Soffit is commonly brush/rolled even when the rest of the house is sprayed. Two reasons: (1) Vented soffits have perforated panels or individual vents — spraying drives paint into attic vent openings, contaminating attic insulation and blocking airflow. (2) Overhead spray creates severe fallout onto the painter and ground surfaces below. Brush/roll avoids both problems. Spray is only appropriate for non-vented (solid panel) soffits where vent contamination is not a risk and when adequate ground protection is in place.
relevant_findings.source: Exterior_Application_Methods_Doctrine.md Part A §6, Part B §1; Exterior_Trim_Systems_Doctrine.md §7 sequencing note

relevant_findings.topic: Vent construction type drives application method constraint
relevant_findings.finding: Vented soffit construction comes in two forms: (1) Continuous perforated panels (vented vinyl or fiber cement soffit panels with factory perforations) and (2) Individual strip vents or circular vents installed in solid panels. Both types present overspray risk into the attic cavity. Non-vented soffit (solid panels or boards) does not have this constraint. The vent_type dimension (vented vs non_vented) controls whether spray is eligible as an application method.

relevant_findings.topic: Height modifier applies to ALL soffit work — soffit is always elevated
relevant_findings.finding: Unlike siding which may be ground-level on single-story buildings, soffit is ALWAYS at eave height. Even single-story homes have soffit at 8-10 ft minimum. Two-story soffit is at 16-20+ ft. The height modifier from Access Staging Doctrine applies to all soffit tasks: ground=1.00 (reachable by hand or short ladder), ladder=1.35, scaffold=1.60, lift=1.50. For soffit, the 'ground' tier only applies to low eaves on single-story porches or ranch-style overhangs reachable without a ladder.

relevant_findings.topic: Soffit is a sheltered surface with lower weathering exposure
relevant_findings.finding: Soffit is protected from direct rain, UV, and the worst weathering by the roof overhang above it. This sheltered position means: (1) lower sheen is acceptable — flat to satin is standard (overhead surfaces show gloss imperfections less, and durability demands are lower); (2) coating longevity is longer than exposed siding or trim; (3) mildew and moisture are the primary degradation mechanisms rather than UV/chalking.

relevant_findings.topic: Vinyl soffit painting is uncommon but valid
relevant_findings.finding: Vinyl soffit panels are typically factory-colored white and never painted. However, painting is valid when: (1) the homeowner wants a color change from factory white; (2) the vinyl has yellowed or discolored from UV exposure; (3) the project requires color coordination with adjacent painted surfaces. When painted, vinyl soffit requires bonding/adhesion primer (e.g., Insl-X STIX, BM Fresh Start) and is subject to LRV restrictions: LRV 55+ for standard paint, LRV 35-40+ with VinylSafe IR-reflective technology.

relevant_findings.topic: Fiber cement soffit (HardieSoffit) follows fiber cement rules
relevant_findings.finding: HardieSoffit panels follow the same rules as HardiePlank siding: factory primer is transit protection only — field prime is REQUIRED before topcoat. Cut edges must be sealed. Back-rolling is AVOIDED on fiber cement (spray-only for factory-smooth finish, when spray is eligible). Alkaline primer required on bare/damaged fiber cement (pH 13.0). Key difference from siding: soffit panels are mounted overhead, so all fiber cement prep and application carries the overhead penalty.

relevant_findings.topic: Wood soffit prep includes knot and tannin management
relevant_findings.finding: Wood soffit (T&G cedar, pine, or plywood) requires tannin bleed management. Cedar and redwood T&G soffit boards bleed tannins through water-based primers. Spot-prime knots with alkyd or shellac-based primer before full field prime with 100% acrylic exterior primer. Plywood soffit panels are less prone to tannin bleed but require edge sealing at panel joints.

relevant_findings.topic: Soffit painted before siding in top-down sequence
relevant_findings.finding: Per Exterior Application Methods Doctrine, correct whole-house spray sequence is top-down: (1) soffits, fascia, gutters FIRST; (2) siding body. This means soffit is painted early in the project sequence. Adjacent fascia and frieze may already be painted or still bare/primed at the time of soffit work. If soffit is painted first, fascia above needs no protection. If fascia is painted first, light masking of fascia during soffit work is needed to prevent roller spatter.

relevant_findings.topic: Soffit often coordinates with porch ceiling
relevant_findings.finding: Soffit and porch ceiling are closely related overhead surfaces. Per PaintScope catalog, they have separate keys (PS_EXT_SURFACE_SF.SOFFIT_FIELD vs PS_EXT_SURFACE_SF.PORCH_CEILING) because porch ceilings are often larger areas with different access characteristics. However, they commonly share the same color and sheen (flat white or light color). When a project includes both soffit and porch ceiling, coordination of color/sheen and scheduling is important.

relevant_findings.topic: Low-pressure washing required for soffit cleaning
relevant_findings.finding: Per Exterior Substrates Doctrine, soffit and trim require low-pressure washing (800-1200 PSI) — significantly lower than siding (1500-3000 PSI). High pressure damages soffit panel edges and thin boards, and forces water into attic cavity through vent openings. Low-pressure garden hose wash with soft brush is the safest approach, particularly for vented soffits.

condition_drivers.impact: Drives primer selection, prep sequence, and application method constraints. Wood: acrylic primer + tannin spot prime. Fiber cement: field prime over factory prime (mandatory). Vinyl: bonding primer + LRV restrictions.
condition_drivers.notes: This is a configuration dimension. Each material has distinct primer and prep requirements.

condition_drivers.impact: Drives primer requirement and prep scope. SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD: full prime required. SS_EXT_PRIMED_FACTORY: field prime over factory prime required (fiber cement). SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD: ready for topcoat, minimal prep.
condition_drivers.notes: SS_EXT_PRIMED_FACTORY is the dominant state for fiber cement soffit NC. SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD is the dominant state for wood soffit NC.

condition_drivers.impact: Controls application method eligibility. Vented soffit: brush/roll only (spray drives paint into attic through vent perforations). Non-vented soffit: spray eligible (no vent contamination risk).
condition_drivers.notes: This is the critical distinction for soffit specs. Vented construction is the majority case in modern residential. Non-vented (solid panel) is less common but exists on specific architectural styles.

condition_drivers.impact: QT2: economy — single coat acceptable on primed surfaces. QT3: standard 2-coat with clean edges. QT4: premium materials, light sand between coats. QT5 is not applicable to soffit field — it is a large-area overhead surface, not fine millwork.
condition_drivers.notes: Per Exterior_Substrates_Doctrine.md §5 — QT5 reserved for fine exterior millwork, not field surfaces.

condition_drivers.impact: Brush/roll is the primary method for vented soffits. Spray is eligible only for non-vented soffits. Brush/roll production rates are significantly lower than spray, but spray on vented soffits is prohibited due to attic contamination.
condition_drivers.notes: Application method is constrained by vent_type. brush_roll is the safe default for all soffit types.

condition_drivers.impact: Height modifier on all tasks at elevation. ground=1.00, ladder=1.35, scaffold=1.60, lift=1.50. Soffit is always at eave height — 'ground' tier only applies to very low single-story eaves (porches, ranch-style overhangs).
condition_drivers.notes: Height modifier stacks with overhead penalty. A 2-story soffit on a ladder has both the 1.35 height modifier AND the overhead work penalty.

quality_differences.description: Economy soffit. Light cleaning (garden hose). Spot prime bare areas only. Single finish coat acceptable on primed surfaces. Economy-grade 100% acrylic exterior flat.
quality_differences.typical_use: Rental property, pre-sale, budget-constrained. Soffit is a low-visibility surface that can tolerate economy treatment.

quality_differences.description: Standard residential soffit. Low-pressure wash. Full field prime on bare wood or factory-primed fiber cement (mandatory). Two finish coats with mid-grade 100% acrylic. Clean edges at fascia and frieze junctions.
quality_differences.typical_use: Standard homeowner NC, most residential soffit painting.

quality_differences.description: Premium soffit. Full low-pressure wash. Field prime with premium primer. Two finish coats with premium materials (SW Emerald, BM Aura). Light sand between coats on visible areas. Inspection under raking light before second coat. Crisp edges at all trim junctions.
quality_differences.typical_use: High-end residential, visible soffits on wide overhangs, deep covered porches where soffit is a prominent visual element.

failure_modes.name: Attic vent contamination from spray application
failure_modes.description: Spray application on vented soffit drives atomized paint into attic cavity through perforated panels or vent openings. Paint clogs vent screens, contaminates attic insulation, reduces attic ventilation capacity, and creates a clean-up liability that far exceeds the cost of the soffit painting itself.
failure_modes.prevention: HARD RULE: Brush/roll only on vented soffits. If spray is used on non-vented soffits, mask all vent openings and individual vents. Never spray toward open vents.
failure_modes.detection: Paint residue visible on attic-side insulation. Vent screens with paint film. Reduced attic airflow.

failure_modes.name: Mildew growth on sheltered soffit surface
failure_modes.description: Soffits are sheltered from direct UV and rain but exposed to moisture condensation from attic temperature differentials. This creates ideal conditions for mildew colonization, especially on north-facing and shaded elevations. Mildew under paint film causes adhesion failure and discoloration.
failure_modes.prevention: Clean soffit with mildewcide solution before painting. Use paint with mildewcide additive. Ensure proper attic ventilation to reduce condensation.
failure_modes.detection: Dark spots or streaks on soffit surface. Musty odor near eave. Paint discoloration in shaded areas.

failure_modes.name: Overhead paint drip and sag
failure_modes.description: Overhead application makes paint drips and sags highly visible and difficult to control. Excess material runs down to fascia junction or drips onto surfaces below. Thicker coats applied overhead are more prone to sag than vertical application.
failure_modes.prevention: Apply thin coats overhead. Use paint formulated for overhead application (higher viscosity, faster tack). Back-brush immediately after rolling to redistribute material and eliminate sag.
failure_modes.detection: Visible drip lines. Sag marks at panel joints. Paint accumulation at fascia-soffit junction.

failure_modes.name: Tannin bleed through on cedar T&G soffit
failure_modes.description: Cedar and redwood tongue-and-groove soffit boards contain water-soluble extractives that bleed through water-based primers and topcoats. Brown or reddish-brown staining appears through the finish coat, especially on knots and end grain.
failure_modes.prevention: Spot-prime knots with alkyd or shellac-based stain blocker before full field prime. Use stain-blocking acrylic primer for full coat. Severe tannin bleed may require two coats of stain-blocking primer.
failure_modes.detection: Brown or reddish-brown discoloration at knots and board junctions. Staining most visible with flat white finish.

failure_modes.name: Thermal distortion on vinyl soffit
failure_modes.description: Dark paint on vinyl soffit absorbs excessive heat, causing PVC panels to warp, buckle, or permanently deform. The heat deflection temperature of standard PVC is approximately 165 degrees F.
failure_modes.prevention: HARD STOP: LRV < 55 on vinyl soffit requires VinylSafe or equivalent IR-reflective technology. Standard dark paint on vinyl is prohibited. Only 100% acrylic latex binders (no alkyd, no oil-based).
failure_modes.detection: Panel warping, buckling, bowing. Gap opening at panel joints. Visible distortion.

failure_modes.name: Edge wicking on fiber cement soffit panels
failure_modes.description: Unsealed cut edges on HardieSoffit panels absorb moisture via cellulose fiber capillaries. Edge swelling ruptures paint film from behind. Overhead position means dripping condensation can pool at panel edges.
failure_modes.prevention: Seal ALL field-cut edges with end-cut sealer or field primer before installation or as early as possible after cutting.
failure_modes.detection: Swollen panel edges. Paint bubbling at cut ends. Visible moisture staining at panel joints.

substrate_analysis.description: Wood soffit — tongue and groove (T&G) boards (cedar, pine, fir) or plywood panels. Porous, hygroscopic substrate.
substrate_analysis.key_properties: T&G boards have many joints creating edge exposure. Cedar and redwood are prone to tannin bleed. Plywood panels are more uniform but have exposed edges at panel joints. Wood soffit absorbs moisture from attic condensation.
substrate_analysis.prep_requirements: Low-pressure wash (800-1200 PSI or garden hose). Sand with 80-120 grit for adhesion profile. Spot-prime knots on cedar/redwood with alkyd or shellac stain blocker. Seal plywood panel edges.
substrate_analysis.primer_type: 100% acrylic exterior primer for field prime. Alkyd or shellac spot-prime for tannin-rich knots on cedar/redwood.

substrate_analysis.description: Fiber cement soffit panels — HardieSoffit. Cementitious composite with factory primer. Non-porous face, porous cut edges.
substrate_analysis.key_properties: Ships with factory primer (transit/weather protection only). Field prime REQUIRED before topcoat per manufacturer warranty. Dense, dimensionally stable. Cut edges absorb moisture via cellulose capillaries. pH 13.0 on bare surfaces.
substrate_analysis.prep_requirements: Low-pressure wash (garden hose — NO pressure washer on soffit panels). Light sand for adhesion profile. Seal all field-cut edges with end-cut sealer.
substrate_analysis.primer_type: Field prime: 100% acrylic exterior primer over factory prime. Alkali-resistant primer (SW Loxon Masonry Primer or equivalent) on bare/damaged fiber cement.

substrate_analysis.description: Vinyl soffit panels — factory-colored PVC. Non-porous, smooth. Typically factory white. Painting is uncommon but valid for color change or discoloration.
substrate_analysis.key_properties: Non-porous dense surface. High thermal expansion. Heat deflection at ~165 degrees F. Factory color means painting voids manufacturer finish warranty. LRV restrictions mandatory — dark colors cause thermal distortion.
substrate_analysis.prep_requirements: Low-pressure wash. Light scuff sand with 220-grit for adhesion profile. Clean with denatured alcohol or TSP to remove static charge and manufacturing residue.
substrate_analysis.primer_type: Bonding/adhesion primer (Insl-X STIX, BM Fresh Start, or equivalent). Must 'bite' into PVC surface through chemical bond.
substrate_analysis.valid_states_note: Vinyl soffit uses SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD state per convention (same prep logic as bare substrate requiring prime). No dedicated SS_EXT_BARE_VINYL state exists.

production_rate_research.source: Exterior_Application_Methods_Doctrine.md, Exterior_Access_Staging_Systems_Doctrine.md, Exterior_Trim_Systems_Doctrine.md, calibrated against sibling exterior specs

overhead_penalty.description: All soffit work is overhead. Overhead position reduces production rates by 25-40% versus equivalent vertical work at the same height. This penalty applies to ALL tasks — prep, prime, and finish.
overhead_penalty.notes: The overhead penalty stacks multiplicatively with the height modifier. Example: 2-story soffit on ladder = base_rate x 0.70 (overhead) / 1.35 (height) = ~52% of ground-level vertical rate.

brush_roll_finish.notes: Brush/roll finish coat on overhead soffit. T&G boards at low end (many joints); solid panels at high end. Includes overhead penalty. Ground-level access.

brush_roll_prime.notes: Brush/roll primer coat overhead. Primer is slightly faster than finish (less precision needed). Ground-level access.

spray_finish_nonvented.notes: Spray finish on NON-VENTED solid panel soffit only. Includes overhead penalty. Back-rolling avoided on fiber cement; optional on wood plywood. Ground-level access.

spray_prime_nonvented.notes: Spray primer on non-vented soffit. Ground-level access.

low_pressure_wash.notes: Garden hose + soft brush overhead. Slower than siding wash due to overhead position and need for care around vents.

spot_prime_knots.notes: Spot-prime individual knots on cedar/redwood T&G soffit. Overhead position reduces rate significantly.

end_seal_fibercement.notes: Brush sealant on cut ends of fiber cement panels. Overhead position reduces rate from the 60-80 EA/hr siding baseline.

caulk_panel_joints.notes: Caulk soffit panel joints overhead. Slower than vertical caulking due to overhead position.

vent_masking.notes: Mask individual vent openings with tape and paper before adjacent work. Small vents are faster; large continuous strips are slower.

modifier_catalog.name: Overhead work penalty
modifier_catalog.description: All soffit tasks carry an overhead work penalty. Applied as a time multiplier (1.35 = 35% more time than equivalent vertical work). This is the soffit spec's defining modifier.
modifier_catalog.stacking: Multiplicative with height modifier (MOD_HEIGHT). Example: overhead 1.35 x ladder 1.35 = 1.82 total modifier.

modifier_catalog.name: Height/access modifier
modifier_catalog.description: Standard exterior height modifier per Access Staging Doctrine. Applied per elevation based on working height.
modifier_catalog.stacking: Multiplicative with overhead modifier. A 2-story soffit on a ladder: overhead 1.35 x ladder 1.35 = 1.82.

modifier_catalog.name: Vented soffit complexity
modifier_catalog.description: Vented soffits require more careful brush/roll technique to avoid driving paint into vent perforations. The 15% penalty applies to finish application tasks on vented soffits. Also adds vent masking tasks when adjacent work (e.g., fascia) is being sprayed.
modifier_catalog.stacking: Multiplicative with overhead and height modifiers.

modifier_catalog.name: Tongue-and-groove joint complexity
modifier_catalog.description: T&G board soffits have many joints (every 3-6 inches) that require brush attention to work paint into grooves. Solid panels (plywood, fiber cement, vinyl) have wider joint spacing. 20% penalty for T&G boards on brush/roll application.

modifier_catalog.name: Surface texture modifier for material consumption
modifier_catalog.description: Rough-sawn plywood or T&G board soffit requires 15% more material per coat versus smooth panel surfaces. Applied to material quantity calculation only.

zones.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to full_cover when application_method = spray (overhead spray creates heavy fallout below)
zones.notes: Landscape/ground directly below soffit work zone. Overhead painting creates drip fallout directly downward. More critical than vertical siding protection because gravity pulls all drips straight down.

zones.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to full_cover when application_method = spray
zones.notes: Walkways and hardscape directly below soffit work area. Drop cloth coverage to catch overhead drips.

Siding field below soffit at wall junction. If siding is already painted, light masking at the soffit-to-siding junction to prevent roller spatter on finished siding. If siding is unfinished (typical in top-down NC sequence), no protection needed.
Fascia above soffit. If fascia is already painted (common in top-down sequence), light masking at fascia-soffit junction. If fascia is unfinished, no protection needed.
Soffit-mounted recessed lights or porch fixtures. Bag or tape over fixture during soffit painting.

protection_zones_analysis.method_escalation: brush_roll < spray (spray creates heavy overhead fallout requiring more ground protection)
protection_zones_analysis.cross_spec_protection_note: Fascia and trim protection during soffit work is handled by adjacency state analysis. If fascia is already finished, this spec adds light masking at the junction. If fascia is unfinished (painted later), no masking needed. This prevents double-counting.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Fascia board is directly above soffit — the soffit panel terminates at or under the fascia. This is the primary cut-in edge for soffit painting. Different color (trim color vs soffit body color) is common. Brush cut-in at this junction is required regardless of application method.
Frieze board is at the soffit-to-siding junction on the wall side. Soffit terminates at the frieze. Different color (trim) typical. Brush cut-in required at this edge.
Siding field below the soffit at the wall plane. Not directly adjacent to soffit (frieze board typically separates them). No cut-in needed — frieze board provides the transition.
Porch ceiling is continuous with soffit in many designs. When continuous, no edge work needed — same surface, same color. When there is a beam or transition, cut-in at the junction.
Rake board at gable ends meets soffit at the eave return. Cut-in needed at this junction. Different color (trim) typical.

adjacency_analysis.key_finding: Soffit has MORE edge work than siding. The fascia and frieze junctions are the primary cut-in lines, and both are overhead. Cut-in labor at these edges is a significant component of total soffit painting time, especially for brush/roll application.

affected_conditions.notes: Height modifier on all soffit tasks. Soffit is ALWAYS elevated — 'ground' tier only applies to very low single-story eaves.

excluded_conditions.rationale: Environmental conditions (wind, dew point, sun exposure, surface temperature) are SOP/process concerns, not estimatable at bid time. They belong in job-site decision protocols, not production rate modifiers. Per sibling spec RC-003 pattern.

excluded.reason: Unpredictable. Less relevant for brush/roll soffit than spray siding.
Soffit is sheltered — less heat buildup than sun-exposed siding.
Weather-dependent. Not predictable at bid time.
Soffit is sheltered by roof overhang. Minimal direct sun.

valid_input_states.rationale: NC soffit has three valid starting states. SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD: new wood T&G or plywood soffit — no coating. SS_EXT_PRIMED_FACTORY: fiber cement soffit (HardieSoffit) with factory primer — field prime required before topcoat. SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD: any substrate already field-primed — ready for topcoat. Vinyl soffit (when painted) uses SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD by convention.

output_state.rationale: Output state is the painted finish. Flat is the most common soffit sheen. Actual output varies by sheen configuration (flat or satin).

adjacent_state_protection_analysis.rationale: Protect finished fascia from soffit roller spatter. Unfinished fascia needs no protection — it will be painted later. In top-down NC sequence, fascia may be painted first.
Protect finished frieze from soffit roller spatter at the wall-side junction.
In top-down sequence, siding is typically unpainted when soffit is done. No protection needed. If sequence is reversed, light masking at wall-soffit junction.

exterior_substrate_states.description: Raw uncoated wood soffit — T&G boards or plywood panels. No primer, no finish.
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Low-pressure wash (garden hose + soft brush). Sand 80-120 grit. Spot-prime knots on cedar/redwood with alkyd/shellac stain blocker.
exterior_substrate_states.primer_type: 100% acrylic exterior primer. Alkyd/shellac spot-prime for tannin-rich knots.
exterior_substrate_states.notes: Primary NC state for wood soffit. Also used as convention state for vinyl soffit painting.

exterior_substrate_states.description: Factory-primed fiber cement soffit panels (HardieSoffit). Factory primer is transit/weather protection only.
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Low-pressure wash (garden hose only). Light sand for adhesion profile. Seal all field-cut edges with end-cut sealer.
exterior_substrate_states.primer_type: Field prime: 100% acrylic exterior primer over factory prime (MANDATORY for warranty compliance)
exterior_substrate_states.notes: Dominant NC state for fiber cement soffit. Field prime is not optional. Must be top-coated within 180 days of installation.

exterior_substrate_states.description: Soffit with field-applied exterior primer — ready for topcoat.
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Light dust-off. Minimal prep — surface is paint-ready.
exterior_substrate_states.notes: Occurs when prime and finish are split across mobilizations or when primer was applied by another crew.

exterior_access_type_analysis.treatment: Modifier on tasks. Identical to FAC_HEIGHT for interior. Stacks with overhead penalty.

scenarios.notes: Low single-story eaves reachable by hand or short stepladder (8-10 ft eave). Uncommon — most soffit requires at least a short ladder.
Standard single-story and two-story soffit. Constant repositioning for overhead work. Safety overhead for overhead ladder work.
Large continuous soffit runs above 12 ft. Scaffold platform allows standing work rather than overhead ladder reaching. Partially recovers overhead penalty through better ergonomics.
Three-story or difficult access. Boom lift positions painter at optimal overhead reach. Best ergonomic outcome for high overhead work.

exterior_access_type_analysis.key_insight: Scaffold and lift partially RECOVER the overhead penalty because they provide a stable platform that allows the painter to stand closer to the soffit surface with better body position. Ladder is the worst combination with overhead work because the painter is both elevated AND reaching overhead from an unstable position.

exterior_environmental_constraints.note: Environmental constraints are documented here for SOP reference but are EXCLUDED from estimation modifiers per established pattern from sibling specs.

sop_reference_only.go_threshold: < 10 mph for spray; brush/roll less sensitive
sop_reference_only.optimal: Calm — overhead brush/roll not significantly affected by wind

sop_reference_only.note: Soffit is sheltered — less heat buildup than sun-exposed surfaces.

sop_reference_only.rule: Surface temp must be >= 5 degrees F above dew point
sop_reference_only.note: Condensation risk on soffit underside, especially early morning.
Check for condensation moisture from attic temperature differential.

notes_for_materials_manager: Three substrate-driven primer paths: (1) Wood: 100% acrylic exterior primer + alkyd/shellac spot-prime for cedar/redwood knots. (2) Fiber cement: 100% acrylic exterior primer as field prime over factory prime (mandatory, not optional). Alkali-resistant primer (SW Loxon) on bare/damaged fiber cement. (3) Vinyl: bonding/adhesion primer (Insl-X STIX, BM Fresh Start).
Finish system: 100% acrylic exterior paint. Flat to satin sheen range. Premium tiers: SW Emerald, BM Aura, or equivalent.
For vinyl soffit, LRV restrictions apply: LRV 55+ standard, LRV 35-40+ with VinylSafe IR-reflective technology. Only 100% acrylic latex binders on vinyl (no alkyd, no oil-based).
Coverage rate for soffit: 250-350 SF/gal per coat on smooth panels. Rough-sawn T&G boards: apply 1.15 surface_factor for material consumption.
End-cut sealer is a separate consumable for fiber cement soffit — needed for all field-cut edges.
Caulk: flexible paintable caulk for soffit panel joints and soffit-to-fascia/frieze junctions.
Consider mildewcide additive or mildew-resistant paint for sheltered soffit surfaces, especially north-facing elevations.
Spray tip for non-vented soffit spray: 413-515 tip. 60-mesh (black) filter for latex.
notes_for_sop_librarian: CRITICAL: Vent type gates application method. Vented soffit = brush/roll ONLY. Non-vented soffit = spray eligible. This is a hard constraint, not a preference.
Module structure: setup -> protect -> clean -> prep -> prime -> apply -> cleanup -> teardown.
All tasks carry overhead work penalty. SOP procedures should note ergonomic best practices for overhead work (frequent breaks, arm fatigue management).
Low-pressure wash ONLY on soffit (800-1200 PSI max, or garden hose + soft brush). High pressure damages panel edges and forces water through vents into attic.
Wood T&G soffit: spot-prime knots with alkyd/shellac stain blocker BEFORE full field prime coat. This is a separate task.
Fiber cement soffit: field prime over factory prime is MANDATORY. Seal all field-cut edges before prime.
Vinyl soffit: scuff sand (220-grit) + degrease + bonding primer before topcoat.
Cut-in at fascia and frieze junctions is overhead brush work. Account for this as a separate task from field rolling.
Top-down sequence: soffit is painted before siding body. Fascia/soffit first, then siding.
When spraying non-vented soffit, mask all vent openings on adjacent vented sections. Never spray toward open vents.
Thin coats overhead. Watch for sag at panel joints and fascia junction.
notes_for_estimation_engineer: Overhead penalty is the defining modifier: all soffit tasks take ~35% longer than equivalent vertical work. MOD_SOFFIT_OVERHEAD = 1.35.
Height modifier stacks multiplicatively with overhead penalty: ladder soffit = 1.35 (overhead) x 1.35 (height) = 1.82 total modifier on base rate.
Brush/roll rates (ground-level, includes overhead penalty): finish 60-100 SF/hr, prime 70-110 SF/hr. These are ALREADY reduced from vertical rates.
Spray rates (non-vented only, ground-level, includes overhead penalty): finish 150-250 SF/hr, prime 180-300 SF/hr.
T&G board soffit: +20% time penalty vs solid panels due to joint complexity (many grooves requiring brush attention).
Vented soffit: +15% time penalty on finish application (careful technique around perforations).
Cut-in at fascia and frieze edges: estimate separately from field coverage. Overhead cut-in is slow — approximately 30-50 LF/hr.
Access modifier: ground=1.00, ladder=1.35, scaffold=1.60, lift=1.50. Applied on top of overhead penalty.
Masking-to-spray ratio for non-vented soffit spray: 2:1 to 3:1 (less masking than siding spray because fewer adjacent surfaces, but ground protection is heavier due to overhead fallout).
Coat system: 1 field prime + 2 finish coats standard for NC. SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD skips prime. QT2 may use single finish coat.
Environmental conditions EXCLUDED from estimation — SOP/process concerns only.
Vent masking task: when spraying fascia or adjacent surfaces, vented soffit openings must be masked. Rate: 15-25 EA/hr for individual vents.

assumptions.value: New construction soffit painting only — enclosed eave underside panels and boards. Does not include fascia, rake, frieze (covered by SF_TRIM_EXT_NC_v1) or porch ceiling (covered by future SF_PORCH_CEILING_EXT_NC_v1).
assumptions.note: Soffit has its own PaintScope key (PS_EXT_SURFACE_SF.SOFFIT_FIELD) distinct from trim and porch ceiling.

assumptions.value: 1.35 (35% slower than vertical work at same height)
assumptions.source: Calibrated from Access Staging Doctrine height degradation data and field experience
assumptions.note: No doctrine document provides an explicit overhead penalty factor. The 1.35 value is derived from the general principle that overhead work is 25-40% slower, calibrated to the midpoint. Flag for field validation.

assumptions.value: Vinyl soffit uses SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD state by convention (same prep logic as bare substrate requiring prime)
assumptions.source: No dedicated SS_EXT_BARE_VINYL state exists in Substrate_State_Reference.md
assumptions.note: May need a dedicated vinyl state in the future. For now, SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD is the closest match (bare substrate requiring bonding primer).

assumptions.value: QT5 not applicable to soffit field
assumptions.note: QT5 reserved for fine exterior millwork. Soffit is a large-area overhead field surface.

assumptions.value: Combined (full phase_scope) — prime and finish in single spec with distinct task IDs per phase
assumptions.note: NC soffit is single-mobilization scope — same crew primes and paints.

uncertainties.detail: The 1.35 overhead penalty factor is derived from general industry guidance (25-40% reduction) calibrated to midpoint. No direct doctrine or production data table provides a soffit-specific overhead factor. The actual penalty may vary significantly with access type — ladder overhead is much more fatiguing than scaffold or lift overhead.
uncertainties.recommendation: Flag MOD_SOFFIT_OVERHEAD = 1.35 for field calibration. Consider splitting into overhead_ladder (higher penalty) and overhead_platform (lower penalty) once field data is available.

uncertainties.topic: Vented vs non-vented proportion in typical NC
uncertainties.detail: The proportion of vented to non-vented soffit on a typical NC residential project is not documented in doctrine. Modern building codes require attic ventilation, so vented soffits are likely the majority case, but some designs use ridge vent only with solid soffits.
uncertainties.recommendation: Default to vented (brush/roll) unless PaintScope explicitly captures vent_type = non_vented.

uncertainties.topic: T&G board spacing impact on production rate
uncertainties.detail: T&G board width varies (3.5 to 5.5 inches typical). Narrower boards have more joints per SF, increasing brush work. The 1.20 modifier is a general estimate — actual impact depends on board width.
uncertainties.recommendation: Use 1.20 as baseline. Field calibration may reveal board-width-sensitive rates.

uncertainties.detail: Vinyl soffit painting in NC context is uncommon — most vinyl soffit is left as factory color. The vinyl substrate path in this spec may rarely be used. However, including it ensures the spec handles the full range of soffit substrates.
uncertainties.recommendation: Include vinyl path but note it as a low-frequency configuration.

key_decisions.decision: Combined (full phase_scope). Prime and finish phases have unique task keys within the single spec.
key_decisions.rationale: NC soffit is a single-mobilization scope — same crew primes and paints. Matches sibling spec pattern. Each phase has its own task IDs and module IDs for independent rate tracking.

Vent type gates application method eligibility (vented = brush/roll only). This is the most important constraint in the soffit spec. It also adds a 15% complexity modifier for finish application on vented soffits.

key_decisions.decision: Include substrate_material dimension: wood, fiber_cement, vinyl
key_decisions.rationale: Each substrate has distinct primer requirements, prep sequence, and failure risks. Drives material system selection.

key_decisions.decision: MOD_SOFFIT_OVERHEAD = 1.35 applied to ALL tasks in this spec. Stacks multiplicatively with height modifier.
key_decisions.rationale: Overhead work is the defining characteristic of soffit painting. Every task is slower overhead. The modifier must be explicit and separate from the height modifier so it can be calibrated independently.

key_decisions.topic: Application method constraint by vent type
key_decisions.decision: Vented soffit: brush_roll ONLY. Non-vented soffit: spray eligible.
key_decisions.rationale: Spray on vented soffit drives paint into attic through perforations — critical failure mode. This is a HARD constraint, not a preference. Non-vented solid panel soffit can safely be sprayed.
QT5 is reserved for fine exterior millwork per Exterior_Substrates_Doctrine §5.4. Soffit is a large-area overhead field surface — not fine-finish work.

key_decisions.decision: Flat to satin. No semi-gloss or gloss.
key_decisions.rationale: Per Exterior_Color_Sheen_Configuration_Doctrine §3: soffits use flat or satin sheen. Overhead surfaces show less gloss benefit, and lower sheen hides overhead application imperfections.

key_decisions.decision: Fascia and trim protection during soffit work is this spec's responsibility. Ground/landscape protection below is this spec's responsibility.
key_decisions.rationale: Soffit work creates overhead drip fallout. Ground protection is critical. Adjacent fascia/frieze masking depends on their finish state at time of soffit application.

key_decisions.decision: EXCLUDED from estimation modifiers. SOP/process concerns only.
key_decisions.rationale: Per established sibling spec pattern. Environmental conditions are unpredictable at bid time.

key_decisions.decision: 1 field prime + 2 finish coats standard for NC at all tiers. SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD skips prime. QT2 may accept single finish coat on primed surfaces.
key_decisions.rationale: Matches sibling spec coat system. Manufacturer warranty compliance requires 2 topcoats on fiber cement. Wood soffit standard is 2 topcoats for durability.

key_decisions.topic: Back-roll policy on fiber cement soffit
key_decisions.decision: Back-rolling AVOIDED on fiber cement soffit (same rule as fiber cement siding). Spray-only finish for fiber cement when spray is eligible (non-vented only).
key_decisions.rationale: Per Application Methods Doctrine Part A §6: fiber cement back-rolling introduces unwanted stipple/orange peel on factory-smooth surface.

key_decisions.decision: LRV < 55 on vinyl soffit requires VinylSafe IR-reflective technology. Standard dark paint on vinyl is PROHIBITED.
key_decisions.rationale: Per Vinyl Aluminum Siding Doctrine §1 and Color Sheen Doctrine §1. Dark colors exceed heat deflection temperature of PVC (~165 degrees F), causing warping.

proposed_new_keys.meaning: Classification of soffit vent construction. Determines whether spray application is eligible.
proposed_new_keys.rationale: This is the critical constraint for soffit spec application method routing. No existing PaintScope key captures this information. Default assumption should be 'vented' (safer — forces brush/roll).
proposed_new_keys.source_method: Collected during exterior scope capture. Visual assessment of soffit panels.

proposed_new_keys.meaning: Classification of soffit panel/board construction. Affects production rate modifier for T&G joint complexity.
proposed_new_keys.rationale: T&G board soffits have 20% higher labor due to joint complexity. This key enables the estimation engine to apply the MOD_SOFFIT_TG_JOINTS modifier.
proposed_new_keys.source_method: Collected during exterior scope capture. Visual assessment.
